speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) how many instances of fire have been reported at indoor and multi-storey car parks in each of the last five years; (b) what are the common causes of these fires; and (c) what are the measures put in place to ensure such fires are tackled and contained in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The annual incidence of such fires remains low.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Car parks in Singapore are required to be designed with fire safety provisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A car park should also be well-ventilated naturally or by mechanical means to dissipate any heat or smoke.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These fire safety measures are regularly maintained and inspected, as required under the Fire Code.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If I heard correctly, he mentioned that none of the fires in the car parks are related to EVs, but as more and more car owners are adopting EVs, I would also want to highlight a concern with the EV chargers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And also, if I remember correctly, the Singapore Civil Defence Force did mention that to put out an EV fire is much harder than a traditional fire.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, have there been experiments or trials to see how our firefighters can do better, should an EV fire happen in multi-storey car parks?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And are there guidelines on where the EV chargers should be installed within a multi-storey car park to better facilitate, especially our firefighters, in combating a fire should it occur?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For example, should chargers be placed only on the ground level of a multi-storey car park?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Yes, we understand that there have been developments, especially in EVs over the years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, our officers and within the fire safety fraternity, there has also been discussion and also guidelines being developed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And the Member also asked about the difference between how much time is taken.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What is key is that we need to play our part, making sure to look out for such instances, where there are items.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, at the same time, there are fire extinguishers available at the Housing and Development Board blocks, and when there are such fires, we should use these.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But also be mindful that there are certain aspects where you just need to call 995 immediately.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are very fortunate today, we have many more people who are first responders and can help to fight fires and to keep our environment and amenities and infrastructures safe.
